name: Honey drops in eyes
lead: Honey drops in eyes is a folk claim that putting diluted honey in the eyes can lighten the iris color. It appears in fringe eye-color discussions and is not an established cosmetic procedure.

Wikipedia's honey article contains little on eye use; it states honey is generally considered ineffective for allergic conjunctivitis [1]. No published studies were found testing honey drops for changing eye color.

General reference sources describe eye color as set by iris pigmentation, and note that over-the-counter lightening drops of other kinds lack proven effectiveness, with the American Academy of Ophthalmology advising against them in 2024 [2][3].

paras: Proponents of the folk remedy say honey has a bleaching or lightening effect that can gradually change eye color. Instructions are not reproduced here.
Eye color is described as depending on iris melanin, and natural shifts occur mostly in infancy and between adolescence and adulthood [3]. No study has reported honey changing iris pigment.

A Grokipedia summary of eye color change attempts says unproven lightening drops carry possible risks including inflammation and infection, and that the AAO advised against them in 2024 [2]. This concerns commercial drops and is not specific to honey.

lore.intro: The claim circulates in fringe eye-color discussions as a home remedy.

claims.claim: Honey drops will lighten your eyes
claims.believers: Proponents say honey lightens pigment gradually when applied regularly.
claims.experts: No published studies have tested this. Related sources report no proven effect for lightening drops and that organisations such as the AAO advise against them [2].

card.summary: A folk claim that honey in the eyes lightens iris color; untested, and related lightening drops are advised against by ophthalmologists.
card.note: Putting non-sterile substances in the eye carries general infection risk.

quick.overview:
Some folk sources say honey drops can lighten eye color.

No studies have tested this, and general references describe eye color as fixed by iris pigment.
quick.mechanism: Proponents claim a gradual bleaching effect. No mechanism has been shown in research.
quick.risks: Non-sterile substances in the eye are generally associated with irritation and infection; the AAO has advised against lightening drops in general.
